ce_bugs.text: minimumTokenResponseSchema computed keys [z.string().toString()] produce garbage literal keys instead of catch-alls, so token-response fields other than access_token are silently stripped
Google path replaces strict googleCredentialSchema.parse with parseRefreshTokenResponse, persisting otherwise-invalid credentials
Salesforce unconditionally refreshes and rewrites the credential on every connection even when the access token is still valid

Webhook endpoint has no HTTP method check (GET accepted)
Webhook secret comparison is non-constant-time
Webhook appId-based credential lookup with findFirst has no type filter or ordering, can update an arbitrary credential when user has both user-level and app-level rows
Webhook update path doesn't update type, so a pre-existing row keeps stale type

Webhook endpoint authenticated only by a shared secret allows overwriting arbitrary app credentials for any userId with no per-request signature, nonce, or user consent (IDOR/credential-injection primitive)
Non-constant-time comparison of webhook secret header creates timing side channel
JSON.parse(symmetricDecrypt(...)) is not wrapped in try/catch, causing unhandled 500s on malformed payloads
Decrypted keys object is never schema-validated (no zod validation) before being persisted as user credential key
Webhook handler doesn't restrict HTTP method to POST, causing unhandled 500 on GET and making mutation reachable via any verb
Fake refresh_token placeholder string 'refresh_token' is written into stored credentials, overwriting the real refresh token
Google path persists the dummy refresh_token via prisma.credential.update, permanently breaking token refresh (data loss)
refreshOAuthTokens doesn't check response.ok, so 4xx/5xx responses are parsed as token responses producing confusing failures
Sync endpoint response is trusted as OAuth token data and persisted as user credentials with weakened validation
Hubspot path types the raw fetch Response as HubspotToken, so refresh_token/expires_in are undefined at runtime, breaking token refresh
Lark's handleLarkError will try to parse the raw Response object in the sync path, breaking Lark token refresh
Salesforce unconditional refresh can corrupt the credential if a failure occurs mid-write, since providers may invalidate rotated refresh tokens
Zoho Bigin passes credentialId where a user id is expected in refreshOAuthTokens, breaking token sync lookup or fetching wrong user's data

parseRefreshTokenResponse.ts:23-25 stores a placeholder refresh_token value ('refresh_token') when the sync endpoint only returns an access token, making local token refresh impossible and forcing per-request sync-endpoint fetches with no dedupe or TTL caching (N+1 pattern under load)
parseRefreshTokenResponse's computed-key zod schema ([z.string().toString()]) doesn't validate 'any numeric property' as intended
refreshOAuthTokens returns a sync-endpoint Response where callers expect provider-specific objects (e.g. Zoho tokenInfo.data, Hubspot typed token), breaking those integrations

Placeholder "refresh_token" string injected by parseRefreshTokenResponse overwrites real refresh tokens when callers spread parsed data over existing credentials, permanently destroying OAuth credentials
Zoho Bigin passes credentialId where refreshOAuthTokens expects the Cal.com userId (calcomUserId), causing wrong user lookup in sharing mode
Outbound credential-sync POST to CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT carries no authentication (no secret header or signature), leaking user ids to an unauthenticated endpoint
Webhook returns 500 on invalid body because appCredentialWebhookRequestBodySchema.parse is not wrapped in try/catch, instead of 400 with zod issues
Salesforce refreshes unconditionally on every service construction and stores only accessTokenParsed.data plus refresh_token as the credential key, dropping previously stored fields

refreshOAuthTokens returns a raw fetch Response when credential sync is enabled, but callers (e.g. zoho-bigin and zohocrm CalendarService accessing tokenInfo.data.error) expect provider-specific shapes, causing TypeError
parseRefreshTokenResponse builds a Zod schema with dynamic key [z.string().toString()] which yields a literal '[object Object]' key instead of 'any numeric property', making validation garbage
Webhook secret compared with !== instead of crypto.timingSafeEqual, enabling timing attacks on CALCOM_WEBHOOK_SECRET which is the sole auth for the credential-overwriting endpoint
Webhook handler uses .parse() which throws on malformed bodies, producing unhandled 500 instead of 400
JSON.parse(symmetricDecrypt(...)) throws if payload isn't valid ciphertext/JSON, unhandled in webhook handler
Webhook handler doesn't check req.method === 'POST', allowing GET/PUT to reach DB mutation paths
No rate limiting on the internet-facing credential-writing webhook endpoint
Salesforce checks success via response.statusText !== 'OK' instead of response.ok; statusText is unreliable (empty for HTTP/2, varies by locale)

Google Calendar CalendarService stores the Zod SafeParseResult wrapper object (from parseRefreshTokenResponse) as the credential key via prisma.credential.update, making the stored credential unreadable by googleCredentialSchema.parse

minimumTokenResponseSchema uses computed keys z.string().toString() which evaluate to a constant instead of a wildcard, breaking the allow-any-property intent and causing safeParse to fail for every legitimate provider response

refreshOAuthTokens uses any typing and returns a raw fetch Response to every caller when the sync branch is active, breaking axios-shaped consumers (zoho-bigin, zohocrm) and hubspot which expect different shapes
Zoho Bigin CalendarService passes credentialId instead of credential.userId to refreshOAuthTokens, so the sync endpoint receives the wrong identifier
Webhook handler app-credential.ts stores the JSON.parse result of the decrypted payload as key without schema validation, and secret comparison uses non-timing-safe string equality
parseRefreshTokenResponse returns the Zod SafeParseReturnType wrapper object which gets stored in credential.key, breaking all downstream access_token reads on the Google Calendar path

parseRefreshTokenResponse force-sets data.refresh_token to the placeholder string "refresh_token", overwriting the user's real refresh token on the Office 365 path and permanently killing the credential

refreshOAuthTokens returns a raw fetch Response in sharing mode while callers expect provider SDK shapes (HubspotToken, axios response, res.data), breaking HubSpot, Zoho CRM, Zoho Bigin, and Google token refresh

Salesforce makes an unconditional refresh call to login.salesforce.com on every service instantiation even when credential sharing is enabled, causing failures because valid credentials are held by the remote app
Salesforce uses response.statusText !== "OK" check which is unreliable for HTTP/2 (empty statusText); should use response.ok
Zoho Bigin passes credentialId as the userId to refreshOAuthTokens instead of credential.userId
Outgoing credential sync request is unauthenticated: no shared secret, signature, or Authorization header, allowing anyone with the endpoint URL to trigger token sync for any user
Webhook handler uses .parse instead of safeParse so malformed input causes unhandled 500 errors
Webhook handler lacks req.method restriction, so GET with garbage body hits the same parse path
Webhook secret compared with plain !== string comparison instead of crypto.timingSafeEqual, vulnerable to timing attacks
minimumTokenResponseSchema computed keys [z.string().toString()]: z.number() produce a single literal key instead of validating numeric properties, so expiry_date/expires_in are never validated

minimumTokenResponseSchema in parseRefreshTokenResponse.ts uses computed keys [z.string().toString()] which evaluate to literal string '[ZodString]', making the schema semantically fabricated and causing safeParse to fail for every legitimate OAuth token response
refreshTokenResponse.data.refresh_token is never declared by either schema and the fallback assigns the literal string 'refresh_token' as the value, producing a bogus persisted key

CalendarService.ts (googlecalendar) persists the SafeParseReturnType wrapper from parseRefreshTokenResponse as the credential key instead of the parsed tokens, permanently breaking the Google credential after one refresh

refreshOAuthTokens.ts returns a fetch Response in sharing mode but callers expect parsed token objects (e.g. res.data, expiresIn, tokenInfo.data), causing crashes or undefined token access in googlecalendar, hubspot, zoho-bigin, and zohocrm

Salesforce CalendarService.ts performs unconditional refresh before connection is constructed; existing credentials without refresh_token in key now send refresh_token=undefined, causing 400 errors and HttpError where jsforce's own refresh flow previously worked
Salesforce salesforceTokenSchema has no refresh_token field so refresh_token: credentialKey.refresh_token can be undefined when persisted
Salesforce CalendarService uses fragile check response.statusText !== 'OK' which fails with locale/proxy-dependent statusText (e.g. empty string on 200 from some proxies)
zoho-bigin CalendarService.ts passes credentialId where every other call site passes credential.userId, potentially a ReferenceError breaking Zoho Bigin if the variable is not in scope

app-credential.ts webhook header lookup uses raw env-driven header name which is case-sensitive against Node's lowercased headers, silently returning undefined and 403-ing all sync webhooks if misconfigured
app-credential.ts header value req.headers[...] can be string[], in which case strict !== comparison against the secret always fails

parseRefreshTokenResponse.ts catchall keys like [z.string().toString()] are no-ops coercing to '[object Object]' instead of a real zod catchall, causing zod to strip all keys except access_token and lose refresh_token, scope, token_type from persisted credentials
parseRefreshTokenResponse.ts sets refresh_token to a placeholder string 'refresh_token' that doesn't exist in any schema, causing invalid-grant failures on next refresh

refreshOAuthTokens.ts shared-mode response is a raw fetch Response object but callers assume a parsed body shape, causing undefined tokens or garbage stored in shared mode (Google, Lark, HubSpot call sites)
zoho-bigin CalendarService passes credentialId instead of credential.userId to refreshOAuthTokens, causing cross-user credential corruption via credential-sync endpoint
app-credential webhook has no HTTP method check and uses zod.parse instead of safeParse on req.body, causing 500s with stack traces on GET or malformed payloads with no rate limit
Request to CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT sends no authentication (no CALCOM_WEBHOOK_SECRET header) and no Content-Type, leaking third-party OAuth credentials to arbitrary callers

symmetricDecrypt and JSON.parse of reqBody.keys in app-credential webhook are unguarded with no 32-byte key length verification, allowing malformed data to be written into credential.key without schema validation
No tests of any kind for the new shared modules (refreshOAuthTokens, parseRefreshTokenResponse, app-credential webhook)

Salesforce CalendarService refresh code bypasses refreshOAuthTokens() and never sources credentials from the sync endpoint even when APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED and CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT are set
Salesforce refresh stores parsed token plus only refresh_token, silently dropping other fields previously in credential.key
parseRefreshTokenResponse discards the app-specific schema when sync is enabled, replacing it with minimumTokenResponseSchema computed with constant string keys that validate essentially nothing
Fabricated literal refresh_token ("refresh_token") is persisted when response lacks one, breaking subsequent refresh cycles; mutation executes in non-sync path too

refreshOAuthTokens returns sync-mode response raw with no validation; callers expect provider-native response shapes and will misparse or crash

Large import churn from file move (_utils/createOAuthAppCredential.ts to _utils/oauth) bundled into feature PR, inflating review surface

minimumTokenResponseSchema uses computed key [z.string().toString()] which evaluates to literal string "[object Object]" instead of a catch-all, so every real OAuth token response fails the parse and credential-sharing mode throws for every app

refreshOAuthTokens returns raw fetch Response in sync mode but callers expect provider-specific shapes (res?.data.access_token, expiresIn, tokenInfo.data.error), breaking all non-Lark providers

When token response has no refresh_token, the literal sentinel string "refresh_token" is written into the credential and later sent to providers as the refresh token, permanently poisoning the credential
Salesforce refresh moved to unconditional upfront fetch in the service constructor path, causing a network token refresh and DB write on every instantiation instead of lazy refresh on expiry
Salesforce uses response.statusText !== "OK" string comparison instead of response.ok/response.status, allowing non-English locales or HTTP/2 reason phrases to pass
zoho-bigin passes credentialId where refreshOAuthTokens signature expects userId (calcomUserId), causing sync to look up/store tokens for the wrong entity

app-credential webhook has check-then-insert TOCTOU: findFirst then create with no unique constraint on (userId, appId), allowing duplicate credentials on concurrent deliveries; needs unique index + upsert or P2002 handling
In sync mode the caller-supplied app schema is discarded and replaced by the weaker minimum schema, so per-app invariants are not enforced and malformed sync responses are written to credential.key
office365calendar error logging removed; when safeParse fails, spreading false is a no-op so old expired credentials are written back and code continues as if refresh succeeded
app-credential webhook lacks HTTP method guard and uses z.parse instead of safeParse, so GET or malformed body throws unhandled ZodError → 500 instead of 400

APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED flag is derived from two env vars but sync behavior also requires CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT checked inline in multiple places; webhook checks only the toggle, allowing credentials stored without refresh path consulting the sync endpoint
